name: Stuff+ Validity
question: Does Stuff+ in season N predict run value in season N+1?
data: Stuff+ from Spin ID's model trained only on 2021-2024 MLB regular-season pitches. Every modeling choice (features, including whether to add accelerations, and settings) is made by accuracy on 2025 alone; 2026 outcomes are not used until this test runs, once.
method: Stuff+ comes from Spin ID's own model, trained only on 2021–2024 pitches. Its settings, and whether to use accelerations, were chosen on 2025 alone.
The test compares 2025 Stuff+ with how the same pitch did in 2026 (run value per 100 pitches), for every pitcher and pitch type with 100+ thrown in both seasons.
Two simpler predictors face the same test: a velocity-only model built the same way, and the pitch's own 2025 run value.
Stuff+ passes only if it lines up with 2026 better than both. Each result has a 95% range from resampling pitchers 2,000 times.

registered_metrics.description: Stuff+ (2025) predicts 2026 run value better than a velocity-only model
registered_metrics.sample: Every pitcher and pitch type with 100+ pitches of that type in both 2025 and 2026 (known pitch types).
registered_metrics.statistic: Pearson r (unweighted, one point per pitcher and pitch type) between each 2025 predictor and the pitch's 2026 run value per 100 pitches (RV/100 = 100 x mean of -delta_run_exp over all 2026 pitches of that type with a run value). The velocity-only model is built exactly like Stuff+ (same three pitch groups, training seasons, batter-side blend, and settings search on 2025) with velocity as its only pitch feature. Passes if r(Stuff+) > r(velocity-only).

registered_metrics.description: Stuff+ (2025) predicts 2026 run value better than 2025 run value does
registered_metrics.sample: Same pitcher and pitch type pairs as above.

gate_rule: The test passes only if both metrics pass. Decisions use the point estimates. Not a gate; the result is shown on Stuff+ wherever it appears.
uncertainty: 95% intervals by bootstrap over pitchers (2,000 resamples, seed 11) for each r and for each difference, reported alongside, not used to decide.

results.value_label: Stuff+'s r minus the velocity-only model's r

reported.description: Stuff+ reliability: odd vs. even games, 2025 (same pairs)
Stuff+ year to year, 2025 vs. 2026 (same pairs)
Each r again, weighted by the smaller of the two seasons' pitch counts
FanGraphs Stuff+ (2025) vs. RV/100 (2026), only if Kade supplies FanGraphs' own export; matched by player and pitch type; never scraped
reported.note: Not supplied (Kade's FanGraphs export not found).

conclusion: Passed. Stuff+ for 2025 lines up with how pitches did in 2026 (r = 0.21) better than a velocity-only model (r = 0.09) and better than the pitch's own 2025 results (r = 0.09). Stuff+ adds information that velocity and last season's outcomes don't.
badge: Validity test T5 passed: Stuff+ in 2025 lined up with 2026 results at r = 0.21, better than velocity alone (0.09) and 2025 results (0.09), over 1,247 pitches.
limitations: One test season (2026) and one model; a different year could come out differently.
Only pitches thrown 100+ times in both seasons count, so rarely used pitches aren't tested.
Run value per 100 pitches is itself noisy over a season, which caps how high any correlation can go.
Stuff+ ignores location and sequencing, which also drive results.
